transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-01-28 08:00 PT | Duration: ~52m | Recording: yes
Attendees (as recorded): Samira P, Jonah K, Alicia R, Tom O, Priya S, Marcus

Summary (auto): Intro + qualification for dedicated reserve; discussed isolation patterns, burst/warm-pool approach, prewarm heuristics, KMS and SOC2 questions. Agreed next steps to share pricing, benchmarks, and sanitized prompt set.

Topics (auto): dedicated capacity, tenant isolation, warm-pool/prewarm, graceful degradation, SLOs, compliance requirements

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samira at Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Jonah from our solutions eng team. 
[00:06] Jonah: Hi all. We'll mostly be listening then digging into the ops and perf questions, feel free to interrupt.
[00:12] Alicia: Thanks - quick intro from our side: I'm Alicia, Head of ML at Vestra Labs, we build a clinical insights assistant. With me are Tom from infra, Priya from security and Marcus product.
[00:22] Tom: Morning.
[00:23] Priya: Hi.
[00:25] Marcus: Hey.
[00:27] Samira: Great. High level, you're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private, right? Where are you leaning?
[00:34] Alicia: We like Redwood hosted for velocity but given PHI-ish data and throughput we might need Dedicated or a Private deployment. Main ask: reserved GPUs for predictable throughput, strong tenant isolation, and ability to handle sudden surges when clinicians run batch analyses.
[00:46] Jonah: Understood. Can you walk us through typical shapes — qps, token lengths, and surge characteristics?
[00:52] Alicia: Median request ~350 tokens, peak 2k for batch reports. Normal RPS is about 20-30, but during morning rounds we spike to 400-600 rps for 10-15 minutes. We're trying to avoid tail-latency > 400ms for short prompts.
[01:09] Tom: Also want ability to isolate certain tenants (PHI customers) onto dedicated nodes; default tenancy needs strict logical separation and audit logs.
[01:18] Priya: And from security: we require KMS integration, customer-managed keys preferred, SAML SSO, SOC2 Type II as baseline. Also we need audit trail retention for 1 year.
[01:29] Jonah: Okay. A few things we usually propose: a Reserved Dedicated pool for steady capacity + a Warm Pool for prewarmed models to handle spikes. We can do tenant fencing so you can pin customers to isolated nodes. For KMS we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in Private and in Dedicated through our integrations — we'll scope exact flow in security session.
[01:46] Marcus: What's the difference vs host'd fallback? If Dedicated is saturated, do requests go to hosted auto-scale?
[01:51] Samira: By policy you can set graceful degradation: fail open to a cheaper model variant in the same pool, or failover to hosted if you accept data routing to Redwood-hosted. For PHI tenants you'd usually avoid that route — you'd prefer a queued/backpressure + retry approach or burst buffer inside your VPC if on Private.
[02:09] Alicia: Hmm, queued backpressure is acceptable for some non-real-time tasks, but for the clinician chat flow we need <500ms.
[02:16] Jonah: So our warm-pool + prefix caching becomes important. If you can keep a few prewarmed workers with KV cache primed for common templates we can hit <200ms for the short prompts. The tradeoff is cost — warm-pool costs more.
[02:30] Tom: How do you size the warm pool? Do you base on median or on historical spikes?
[02:35] Jonah: It's a mix. We look at percentiles — 95th or 99th depending on your SLO. For example: if spikes are 600 rps for 10 minutes, you don't want to reserve 600 rps 24/7. Instead we model: reserve baseline (say 100 rps) + warm pool sized for expected concurrent tokens during spike windows and autoscale ramp rate. We also simulate startup prewarm time for models — big models can take tens of seconds to load unless warm.
[02:59] Alicia: Can you quantify costs? We gave some numbers in the RFP but want an example: baseline reserved for 100 rps + warm pool that handles +500 rps for 15 minutes a day.
[03:11] Samira: We'll provide an example pricing scenario. High-level: reserved nodes priced monthly, warm-pool a smaller hourly commitment. Jonah will run cost sim after we get your exact token distribution.
[03:22] Marcus: What about eviction and isolation — if a warm-pool is shared across tenants, is there risk of cross-tenant leakage?
[03:29] Jonah: Good question — by default pools are multi-tenant with strong software isolation. For PHI you'd pick dedicated nodes and tenant fencing so models and KV caches are assigned to your tenant slice. Warm-pool can be per-tenant or per-customer. There's also an ephemeral per-request containerization option in Private.
[03:45] Priya: On auditability: are audit logs forwarded to our SIEM? Can we integrate with CloudWatch / Splunk?
[03:50] Samira: Yes, we have log-forwarding integrations and can push audit events to your SIEM, and also provide full request/response hashes (redacted) for forensic. For compliance we can do increased retention for logs as an addon.
[03:59] Tom: Latency-wise, what's typical for a dedicated reserved GPU node with warm pool for 350-token prompts?
[04:05] Jonah: For a 350-token request on an optimized LLM variant with KV cache hit and warm worker, median is ~120-220ms token streaming; end-to-end depends on client-side too, but usually within your <500ms for short prompts. For long batch 2k tokens it's obviously higher — we're talking seconds.
[04:22] Alicia: We often use quantized LLMs for cost reasons — does Redwood support q8/q4 fuzz quantization in dedicated?
[04:28] Jonah: Yes, the runtime supports multiple quantization paths and we can recommend models + quantization. There's a small quality delta for aggressive quantization; Redwood Optimize will surface recommendations and tradeoffs per workload.
[04:39] Marcus: About fallback — if the model variant degrades quality during fallback to cheaper model, how do we monitor/alert for regressions?
[04:45] Samira: We have quality monitoring tied to your evals/prompt sets. If fallback triggers, our regression alerts notify you and we can auto-roll back to previous model or route to a canary. You can set thresholds based on perplexity/ROUGE or custom human-labeled checks.
[04:58] Tom: Wanted to ask about preemption — if we reserve nodes, will they ever be preempted for higher-tier customers?
[05:03] Jonah: Dedicated reserved nodes are not preempted; the only times we'd move workloads is during maintenance windows or with explicit agreement. For burst instances (non-reserved) eviction can occur.
[05:10] Alicia: For Private deployments, does Redwood still manage the control plane? We're evaluating a customer-managed control plane too.
[05:16] Samira: In Private mode you get a customer-controlled compute plane. There's an option for Redwood-managed control plane or a full customer-managed control plane depending on the contract and on-prem constraints.
[05:25] Priya: We need to review where keys are stored — is KMS only for private?
[05:29] Jonah: For Dedicated we integrate with major KMS providers (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault) and can do customer-managed keys. For Private on-prem you can plug into your HSM. We'll get details in the security session.
[05:39] Marcus: Anything on networking? We need VPC peering and private connectivity, limits on egress?
[05:44] Samira: Yes we support VPC peering, PrivateLink-like tunnels, and configurable egress rules. Also egress auditing and data residency controls.
[05:52] Tom: On the ops side, how do we manage rollouts — can we do canary between model versions in dedicated pool?
[05:58] Jonah: Absolutely. Canary deployments and traffic splitting are in the Console. You can route a percentage of traffic to a canary, run evals, then promote. We also support auto-fallback policies if latency or error rates rise.
[06:10] Alicia: A concern: our peak pattern is short but frequent. Will warm-pool spinning up every 10 minutes cause thrash?
[06:16] Jonah: That's where conservative autoscale windows help — set a cooldown and keep minimal warm capacity for expected windows. Also prefix caching reduces the need for full model warm-up if prompts share prefixes.
[06:29] Priya: For data handling, when failover to hosted occurs, what data residency guarantees change?
[06:36] Samira: If you enable failover to hosted, requests will transit our hosted region — that may violate your residency constraints. For PHI tenants we typically disable cross-route failover.
[06:45] Marcus: One more: Can we run chaos tests — simulate node failure and observe graceful degradation?
[06:50] Jonah: Yes, we can do a tabletop + live chaos run in a staging dedicated pool. We'll provide a playbook for resilience testing.
[06:57] Alicia: Good. What should we expect in the pricing doc? Will you give monthly amortized numbers with warm-pool hourly?
[07:03] Samira: We'll give a sample with assumptions: reserved monthly, warm-pool hourly/day, cost per token estimates, and a sensitivity analysis for different spike shapes.
[07:12] Tom: Ok. On the timeline — we want to pilot in 6 weeks. Is that feasible?
[07:16] Jonah: Yes — pilot typically 4-8 weeks: onboarding, traffic replay, latency bench, tweak configs. If you provide prompt sets and a traffic export quickly we'll compress to ~4-6 weeks.
[07:26] Priya: For the security deep-dive, can you include Redwood's incident response and pen test reports?
[07:30] Samira: We'll include SOC2, recent pentest summary, and our incident response runbook.
[07:36] Marcus: Any gotchas with model quantization on dedicated nodes?
[07:39] Jonah: Just quality vs speed tradeoff and kernel availability per GPU type. We'll recommend quantization profiles matched to your model and GPU.
[07:47] Alicia: Alright, recap then next steps?
[07:50] Samira: Recap: Vestra needs predictable reserved capacity with warm-pool for short spikes, tenant fencing for PHI tenants, KMS customer-managed keys, SAML SSO, and audit log forwarding. Redwood will provide pricing scenarios, a latency/cost benchmark with Vestra prompts, and schedule a security deep dive.
[08:06] Tom: Sounds right.
[08:07] Priya: Yes.
[08:08] Alicia: Thanks, appreciate it.
[08:10] Samira: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and set the security session.
[08:14] Jonah: I'll kick off the bench once we get the prompt set.
[08:17] Marcus: Cheers.

Auto-generated action note: pricing doc will include three scenarios (baseline reserve only; reserve + warm-pool; private deployment). Jonah to attach spreadsheet with latency/cost sim.

End of meeting.
